statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
A root-to-leaf path starts at the root and follows child links down to a leaf, a node with no children.
Return every root-to-leaf path, each written as its values joined by "->". List the paths from left to right, in the order a depth-first search that tries the left child first reaches their leaves.

examples.explanation: 2 has only a right child, 5, and 3 is a leaf. That gives two leaves, and so two paths.
The tree is full with four leaves, 4, 5, 6 and 7, and each gives one path.
